A cobblestone square shimmers under a canopy of cherry blossom, pale petals drifting past stalls hung with woven baskets and bundles of dried roses, a couple in matching scarves leaning close over a tray of sugared pastries as the soft spring light pools gold across the striped awning cloth.

A shōtengai in late-afternoon gold runs its length beneath a vaulted roof of pale fabric awnings, crates of persimmon and earthy burdock root lining each side, steam curling from a small grilled-rice stall at the far end while a shopper with a deep bamboo basket pauses to choose among the mushrooms.

A wide market square settles into the blue calm of early evening, lanterns just beginning to warm along the bunting-strung eaves, crates of late-summer tomatoes and sunflowers crowding each stall as a vendor in a striped apron rearranges a towering pyramid of peaches and a butterfly hovers close.

A narrow roadside michi-no-eki stall glows beneath a row of round paper lanterns in the golden dusk, its trestle tables laden with bundled satsuma, dried persimmon, and woven bags of new rice, a couple sharing a quiet word beside the stall as potted autumn marigolds line the earthen path at their feet.

A cobblestone market lane stretches its full cheerful length under summer sun, striped awnings fluttering above hanging herb bundles and towers of berry crates, a shopper in a soft linen shawl trailing her hand along a basket of lavender while a small ginger cat naps, perfectly round, atop a flour sack.

A shōtengai at high noon glows with the cool green light filtering through its plain fabric roof, crates of fat daikon, jade-green sudachi, and clusters of enoki arranged in careful plenty beneath each stall, a vendor in a neat dark apron bowing warmly to a shopper whose wide basket is already heaped with good things.

A cobblestone town square blooms under golden midday light, striped awnings in cream and sage sheltering crates of strawberries and fat cabbages, a shopper in a floral apron pausing to lift a jar of honey while bunting flutters overhead and a tortoiseshell cat naps on a sun-warmed crate.

A narrow shōtengai glows beneath strings of round paper lanterns at late afternoon, plain undyed canvas awnings lining the covered street above crates of pale daikon and glossy eggplant, a vendor in a indigo work jacket carefully arranging mushrooms while potted ferns crowd the stall edges and steam curls from a nearby food stand.

A packed-dirt market square basks in soft summer morning light, its stalls draped with cheerful yellow-and-white awnings and heaped with lavender bundles, jars of preserves, and braided garlic, a couple in linen shirts browsing slowly while climbing roses trail across the wooden stall frames above them.

A countryside roadside stall stands beneath a broad wooden lean-to roof in fresh spring light, rough-hewn crates overflowing with satsuma and foraged mushrooms crowding the counter, a shopper in a quilted vest reaching for a bundle of green onions as a pale butterfly drifts through the open front and potted pansies line the path.

A wide town square sparkles under a clear midsummer sky, every stall wrapped in red-and-white striped canvas and loaded with watermelons, sunflowers in tin buckets, and baskets of blueberries, a vendor in a broad straw hat cheerfully fanning out a display of woven baskets while petals from a flowering plum tree drift softly across the cobblestones.

A shōtengai side street hushes into golden-hour warmth, its rows of plain ecru fabric awnings casting long soft shadows over crates of persimmons and bundles of dried chrysanthemum, a pair of shoppers sharing a small cloth bag pausing to admire a vendor's careful pyramid of yuzu while potted bamboo lines the alleyway entrance.

A cobblestone market square glows in the slant of early evening sun, hanging baskets of trailing nasturtiums and ivy bracketing each stall where rounds of farmhouse cheese and braided loaves sit beside copper pots of wildflower honey, a young shopper in a red knit cardigan reaching up to smell a bunch of dried lavender as a tabby cat weaves lazily between her boots.

A michi-no-eki timber lean-to catches the cool light of an overcast spring morning, its low wooden shelves brimming with fat shiitake, bundles of warabi fern, and neatly stacked satsuma in wooden trays, a vendor in a pale grey apron and rubber boots arranging daikon in careful rows while paper lanterns hung from the rafters glow faintly warm in the dim.

A bustling town square unfurls under a canopy of pink cherry blossom at the height of spring, its market stalls threaded with pastel bunting and piled with tulip bunches, asparagus, and fresh herb pots in terracotta, a couple with a wicker basket pausing at the flower stall as petals drift like soft snow across the cobblestones around their feet.

A shōtengai covered street stretches into warm late-morning haze, plain warm-white fabric awnings rippling gently above crates of mountain mushrooms, deep-purple eggplant, and glossy green shishito, a shopper in a plaid wool shawl lifting a daikon to inspect it while a small marmalade cat sits between two crates blinking slowly in a patch of slanted sunlight.
